title: Edge-proximity routing onboarding illustration pack
creator: Marina Ortega
description: Design a set of onboarding and quickstart visuals that explain Redwood's region and latency routing behavior to new users. The pack should include static explainer diagrams, map-based visuals illustrating edge proximity and multi-region failover, a set of small-screen onboarding cards for the Console, and final product screenshots annotated for docs. Focus is on clarity for engineers and platform teams: what routing decision is made, why latency matters, and how to configure routing policies (latency-first, cost-first, region-preference, failover).
deliverables: Hero explainer diagram (wide horizontal) showing routing policy decision tree and latency bands
Interactive-ready SVG map layers (3 breakpoints: desktop, tablet, mobile) with color tokens and labeled nodes
Onboarding card set: three-step microcards for Console quickstart (Proximity, Policy, Fallback)
Annotated product screenshots for docs: routing policy dropdown, latency histogram, model fallback modal
Two short looping Lottie animations for docs: (1) live request path showing TTL + KV cache hits, (2) failover waterfall across regions
acceptance_criteria: All visuals reviewed and approved by PM and Eng with sign-off comments resolved
SVG map exported with accessible color palette (contrast ratio >= 4.5:1) and tokenized colors
Screenshots match Console state for release-2025.11 and include captions + alt text
Assets exported as vector SVGs and PNGs at 1x and 2x; Lottie JSONs validated in dev sandbox
Figma file contains named components, auto-layout frames for responsive breakpoints, and an assets page with export presets
progress_updates: 2025-11-04: Kickoff with PM and Runtime Eng. Agreed scope and prioritized deliverables.

2025-11-06: Initial wireframes created — rough hero diagram and three microcard concepts posted to Figma (link below). Requested latency bands be simplified to three buckets: low (<30ms), medium (30-120ms), high (>120ms).

2025-11-08: Engineering review with runtime team. Samir collected kernel-scheduling screenshots and latency histogram to use as background pattern. Decision: use simplified polyline map rather than full topo map to reduce visual noise.
2025-11-10: First visual pass completed. Shared with PM (Ava Chen) and Design Lead (Diego Morales). Feedback: reduce color saturation, add explicit failover arrows, include small-screen layout.
2025-11-13: Implemented feedback; added Lottie storyboards and export tests. PR opened for docs inclusion: GitHub.com/redwood-inference/docs#PR-3145.
2025-11-15: Accessibility pass complete. Preparing final assets and annotated screenshots for release notes.
review_feedback: Ava Chen (PM): Emphasize tradeoffs between latency and cost; add microcopy for the Console quickstart that surfaces estimated cost delta.
Diego Morales (Design Lead): Use tokenized colors and ensure iconography aligns with System v3. Add alternative map for colorblind users (pattern overlays).
Nora Li (Runtime Eng): Requested that hero diagram show KV cache behavior and a fallback path to a smaller quantized model — added as a dashed secondary path.
Sam Thompson (Docs): Ask for screenshot captions and alt text strings to be delivered in this ticket so docs can embed assets without waiting for copy.
notes: Map approach: abstracted vector polylines over muted world tile to keep focus on request paths rather than geography.
Color tokens selected: --rw-blue-500, --rw-teal-400 (proximity), --rw-amber-500 (medium latency), --rw-rose-600 (high latency). Provided a pattern overlay for colorblind accessibility.
Export specs: SVG sprite for web, 2x PNG for docs, Lottie JSON for two micro-animations; provide a static GIF fallback for email release notes.
Localization: ensure microcard copy fits 140 characters for all supported locales; plan separate task for translation strings.
